# An ambient simplex defeats the endpoint-centroid-midpoint rule

There is an actual six-dimensional simplex with three positive
integer fibers, none carrying half the mixed mass, for which the
midpoint of the two endpoint-fiber centroids has mixed depth
STRICTLY BELOW Gamma_5/2. The midpoint is an actual point of the
middle fiber. A single explicit ambient cap certifies the failure.

This refutes a natural endpoint-centroid gluing rule in the ambient
simplex class. It does not refute OC or the distinct rule using the
own centroid of the middle fiber.

## 1. Exact ambient simplex and positive fibers

Use coordinates (z,x_1,...,x_5), with z the unchanged integer base,
and let C be the simplex with seven vertices
\[
 (0,0),\ (4,0),\ (0,e_1),\ (0,e_2),\
 (1,e_3),\ (3,e_4),\ (3,e_5).                        \tag{1}
\]
The height multiset is (0,0,0,1,3,3,4). The vertices are affinely
independent: the two zero-continuous-coordinate vertices span the
base direction and the remaining continuous coordinates are the
standard basis. Its ambient volume is V=4/6!=1/180.

The exact normal form is
\[
 x\ge0,\quad \sum_i x_i\le1,\quad
 x_3+3x_4+3x_5\le z
 \le4-4x_1-4x_2-3x_3-x_4-x_5.                       \tag{2}
\]
Thus the integer fibers with positive five-dimensional volume are
exactly K_1,K_2,K_3. At base zero the fiber is a two-dimensional
triangle; at base four it is a point. They have zero five-volume
and contribute no mass. There are no additional integer bases.

The slice formula in
candidate 56a670ccbde263ec
gives, for 0<=s<=4,
\[
 \frac{w(s)}V=
 \frac{(4-s)_+^5}{32}
 -\frac59(3-s)_+^4+\frac1{18}(3-s)_+^5
 -\frac12(1-s)_+^5.                                 \tag{3}
\]
Outside the interval the density is zero. The endpoint values at
zero and four are zero, consistent with their lower-dimensional
actual fibers. Equation (3) can also be obtained directly by
confluent divided differences at 0 repeated three times and
3 repeated twice.

In particular
\[
 \frac{(w_1,w_2,w_3)}V
       =\left(\frac{139}{288},\frac12,\frac1{32}\right),
 \qquad \frac MV=\frac{73}{72}.                      \tag{4}
\]
The normalized weights are
\[
                    \frac1{292}(139,144,9).
\]
All three are positive and strictly less than one half. Hence base
two is the unique weighted median of the positive base masses.

There is even exact midpoint compatibility:
\[
                         K_2=(K_1+K_3)/2.          \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, clipping C to 1<=z<=3 produces no vertices with base strictly
between 1 and 3: the original vertices have heights 0,1,3,4, and all
new clipping vertices lie on the clipping planes. The slab is
therefore the convex hull of its two boundary fibers, proving (5).

## 2. The deterministic candidate is feasible

Let g_j be the true ordinary centroid of K_j. The duplicated-knot
moment formula from the same source gives their continuous coordinates.
For explicit computation use the vertex order of (1), with knots
\[
                 h=(0,4,0,0,1,3,3).
\]
If \(f_h(s)=w(s)/V\), the normalized barycentric moment is
\[
 \frac1V\int_{K_s}\lambda_i\,dx
       =\frac17 f_{h\mathbin{\uplus}\{h_i\}}(s),\qquad
 \lambda_i(g_s)=
       \frac{f_{h\mathbin{\uplus}\{h_i\}}(s)}{7f_h(s)}.
                                                               \tag{6a}
\]
Here the duplicated-knot density is computed by the same confluent
divided difference, now with eight knots and exponent six. In
particular the five continuous coordinates are the last five
barycentric moments divided by \(w(s)\). They are
\[
 \begin{split}
 g_1&=\left(
 \frac{5801}{30024},\frac{5801}{30024},\frac16,
 \frac{227}{2502},\frac{227}{2502}\right),\\
 g_3&=\left(\frac1{24},\frac1{24},\frac1{18},
                                      \frac16,\frac16\right).
 \end{split}                                                   \tag{6}
\]
Each is the centroid of a positive actual fiber, not an ambient
projection centroid. Consider the endpoint-centroid-midpoint rule
\[
 y=\left(2,\frac{g_1+g_3}{2}\right)
  =\left(2,\frac{1763}{15012},\frac{1763}{15012},
                  \frac19,\frac{161}{1251},\frac{161}{1251}\right).
                                                               \tag{7}
\]
Convex compatibility, or (5), implies y belongs to K_2, so it is an
admissible point of C intersect (Z x R^5).

Let lambda_* be the barycentric coordinate of the unique height-four
vertex (4,0). By (2),
\[
              \lambda_*(z,x)=
                  \frac{z-x_3-3x_4-3x_5}{4}.
\]
The endpoint centroids have
\[
 \lambda_*(g_1)=241/3336,\qquad
 \lambda_*(g_3)=35/72.
\]
Consequently
\[
                  \lambda_*(y)=1397/5004>1/4.       \tag{8}
\]
These identities can be verified from (6) directly. They also follow
from the corresponding duplicated-knot moments, so both the center
normalization and its base have been checked.

## 3. One exact ambient cap defeats the rule

Take the fixed closed ambient halfspace
\[
 H=\{\lambda_*\ge1/4\}
   =\{z-x_3-3x_4-3x_5\ge1\}.                        \tag{9}
\]
By (8), y is strictly inside H. This is a valid depth test even
though its boundary need not pass through y. Its continuous normal
is nonzero, so its boundary has zero five-volume in each positive
fiber.

The canonical cap formula gives
\[
 \frac{\mu_C(H)}V
  =\left(\frac34\right)^5
    \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}
        \frac{w((j-1)/(3/4))}V.
\]
Only the bases j=2,3 contribute positive volume. The arguments at
j=1 and j=4 are the zero-volume endpoint levels 0 and 4; all other
arguments are outside the source. Therefore, using (3),
\[
 \begin{split}
 \frac{\mu_C(H)}V
 &=\left(\frac34\right)^5
       \left[\frac{w(4/3)}V+\frac{w(8/3)}V\right]\\
 &=\frac{559}{3072}.                                \tag{10}
 \end{split}
\]
The normalized cap mass is
\[
                   \frac{\mu_C(H)}M
                    =\frac{1677}{9344}.
\]
It is strictly below the mixed target:
\[
 \frac{\Gamma_5}{2}
      -\frac{1677}{9344}>0,\qquad
 \Gamma_5=\left(\frac56\right)^5.
\]
Equivalently, the exact absolute deficit is
\[
 \frac{\Gamma_5M/2-\mu_C(H)}V
                      =\frac{48739}{2239488}>0.     \tag{11}
\]
Thus the mixed depth at the actual point y is at most about 0.179473,
whereas Gamma_5/2 is about 0.200939.

A sharper through-y cap lambda_*>=1397/5004 has normalized mass
4150356952177626013/28629870146058409344, about 0.144966,
but the simpler fixed cap (9) already proves the desired failure.

## 4. The own middle centroid: all canonical orientations

The distinct candidate at base two has barycentric coordinates,
in the order of (1),
\[
 \lambda(g_2)=
 \left(\frac{25}{243},\frac5{27},
       \frac{25}{243},\frac{25}{243},\frac7{54},
       \frac{61}{324},\frac{61}{324}\right).          \tag{12}
\]
They follow exactly from (6a) with \(s=2\); their sum is one and
their height-weighted sum is two. Thus the continuous coordinates are
\[
 g_2=\left(\frac{25}{243},\frac{25}{243},\frac7{54},
                                      \frac{61}{324},\frac{61}{324}\right).
\]
For each ambient vertex \(i\), the through-centroid canonical upper cap
is \(H_i^+=\{\lambda_i\ge\lambda_i(g_2)\}\). Put
\[
 Q_i(c)=\frac{(1-c)^5}{73/72}
       \sum_{j=0}^4 f_h\!\left(\frac{j-ch_i}{1-c}\right).
                                                               \tag{13}
\]
The canonical cap formula evaluates every cap, including any zero
endpoint contributions. The four symmetry-distinct answers are:

| Vertex height | Multiplicity | Threshold \(c\) | Exact normalized mass \(Q_i(c)\) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| \(0\) | 3 | \(25/243\) | \(1208406711707/2290817351457\) |
| \(1\) | 1 | \(7/54\) | \(59476257373/134076187008\) |
| \(3\) | 2 | \(61/324\) | \(31539470594257/115841825574912\) |
| \(4\) | 1 | \(5/27\) | \(96895537/349156737\) |

Their approximate values are \(0.527500,\ 0.443600,\ 0.272263,\)
and \(0.277513\), respectively. Exact rational comparison gives
\[
               \Gamma_5/2<Q_i(c)<1-\Gamma_5/2
                      \quad\hbox{for every }i.     \tag{14}
\]
Each \(\lambda_i\) has a nonzero continuous linear part. Its level
hyperplane therefore has zero five-volume in every positive fiber.
Consequently the complementary through-centroid orientation
\(H_i^-=\{\lambda_i\le\lambda_i(g_2)\}\) has normalized mass
\(1-Q_i(c)\). Equation (14) checks all fourteen canonical orientations.

These calculations do not refute the own-middle-centroid rule on
this source. They also do not prove that rule: an arbitrary ambient
halfspace need not be one of these fourteen caps.

## 5. Scope

The simplex (1) is full dimensional, the source is measured with
full five-dimensional fiber volume, all three positive fibers are
retained, and no fiber is half-heavy. Equation (5) also rules out
attributing the failure to an independently enlarged middle fiber.
The obstruction is the specific midpoint of endpoint centroids.

No bound below the target has been proved for every candidate.
In particular this note does not claim that the own middle-fiber
centroid fails, or that C violates OC. Canonical caps are used only
to refute one named candidate; they are not claimed to suffice for
an all-halfspace lower bound.

The exact verifier
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_simplex_endpoint_centroid_midpoint_failure.py checks (2)-(14), the slice and
moment formulas, all actual cap contributions including closed
endpoint levels, and the nonheavy inequalities. The numerical
search that located this example is not part of the proof.
